title: Convergent traffic shedding and graceful stream handoff for active-active edge
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Hosted API customers occasionally see user-visible disruptions during region outages and capacity spikes. For short RPCs we have graceful failover; for long-lived streaming/chat sessions (persistent HTTP/WS streams and tokenized continuation flows) users experience abrupt disconnects or inconsistent duplicate messages when traffic is shifted between regions. We need an active-active traffic strategy that preserves SLOs (latency and availability), enforces region-level circuit-breakers, and applies deterministic load-shedding to protect tail latency while minimizing session loss.

Goal: Implement a convergent design that combines region-aware circuit breakers, workload-aware shedding, and a two-phase streaming handoff to minimize user impact during region failover or load-driven eviction. Deliver configuration defaults and automation for the hosted edge and a verification suite that proves end-to-end continuity and SLO adherence under failure scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Region-level P95 latency SLO (120ms for text gen, 250ms for streaming handshake) and error-rate SLO (<=0.2% 5xx) are enforced and visible in dashboards for both regions
A2: Circuit breaker policy that trips on sustained error-rate >5% over 1 minute or CPU/GPU saturation exceeding 85% prevents new sessions being routed to the degraded region

A3: Load-shedding policy that evicts low-value traffic (background embeddings, bulk batched requests) when per-edge queuing exceeds 250ms impact on P95 successfully reduces tail latency by >=20% in load tests

A4: Streaming handoff succeeds for >=98% of in-flight streams when a region is gracefully drained (canary and emergency drain) — user-observed reconnects limited to <=2s median, with a documented continuation token flow to resume generation without duplications
A5: Automated chaos tests (region blackhole, network partitions, spike shear) run in CI and assert SLOs and session continuity thresholds are met
A6: Runbook and console controls to initiate and abort region drain operations are available to SREs and on-call engineers
tasks: T1: Finalize circuit-breaker thresholds and backoff windows (proposal v1 in links)
T2: Implement per-route dynamic shedding rules in gateway with priorities (interactive vs background)
T3: Add dual-write ephemeral session tokens and in-flight dedup IDs to streaming runtime
T4: Implement short-window ‘mirror-and-cutover’ handoff: mirror last N seconds to target region, then atomically cut traffic using consistent routing key
T5: Extend telemetry: region inflight-count, queue-delay-95, kv-sync-lag, dedup-miss-rate
T6: E2E tests: simulate region outage and measure reconnect time and message continuity
T7: Documentation: runbook, console UI copy, and rollout checklist
T8: Create canary plan and automated rollback hooks tied to SLO regressions
implementation_notes: Design decision: use a conservative default circuit-breaker (5% 5xx over 60s) + burst allowance; make thresholds configurable per-customer tier
Sticky session model: do not depend on IP affinity — use an opaque session-id that is routable via consistent hashing to prefer primary region and allow deterministic failover to secondary region
Streaming continuation: include stream-position and dedup-id in each chunk; target region replays omitted chunks by idempotent resume API
KV sync: leverage async kv-replication with bounded TTL (30s) for session metadata to reduce failover window; handoff mirrors last 10s of KV updates
Mirror strategy: for graceful drains, gateway will enter mirror mode for 15s where source region forwards copies to target region’s runtime to prewarm KV and caches

Load-shedding priorities: interactive chat > structured output/extraction > embeddings > bulk batch; shedding triggers use combined signal (queue-delay, GPU active percentage, circuit trip probability)
Edge runtime change: introduce per-request 'evictable' flag so downstream schedulers can preempt lower-priority work when under pressure
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal canary — route 1% traffic for non-critical orgs with new gateway flags enabled (1 week)
Phase 1: Beta customers opt-in (10%) and run targeted load tests (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 50% with automated SLO guards and rollback on regressions
Phase 3: Default enable for hosted API with guardrails and 2-week monitoring window
test_plan: Unit tests for circuit-breaker state machine and shedding selector
Integration tests for dual-write token lifecycle and dedup behavior
Chaos: region-blackhole, high-latency links, CPU/GPU saturation to validate shedding and failover
Load test: synthetic workload that mixes 60% short interactive requests + 40% long streams and bulk batches; assert latency p95 and session continuity metrics
Canary telemetry assertions: no >10% regression in cost-per-token or >0.1% increase in 5xx across canary window
monitoring_and_alerting: SLO dashboards per-region and per-route (latency P50/P95/P99, 5xx rate, inflight-streams)
Alert: circuit-breaker entering ‘open’ state in a region (P0) — notify on-call and mute non-essential ingestion
Alert: queue-delay-95 > 250ms for >2 minutes — trigger automated shedding policy
Alert: kv-sync-lag > 500ms — possible stream handoff risk
Synthetic probes: periodic end-to-end streaming probe that asserts reconnect < 2s and no duplicates
